implementation_summary: EV-0006 dead-links timeout was a full-suite load artefact: standalone the test passes in about 24-25 s (bound unchanged, still 30000 ms), crawl bounded, 500/403 in skipped. The first standalone run exposed a different failure, the LC-001 politeness-note test, caused by RobotsPolicy.fetch now using public-only makeOutboundFetch (ADR 0031) so the localhost fixture's robots.txt is refused and the policy becomes allow-all. Fixed in the test by spying RobotsPolicy.fetch to run the real fetch with an allowPrivate:true outbound fetch (reason commented), plus vi.restoreAllMocks() in finally. No assertion weakened, no test removed or skipped. sessionsOf() confirmed working.

risks: The dead-links test takes about 24-25 s against a 30000 ms timeout, so only about 5 s of margin. It can time out again on a loaded machine. I did not isolate what makes it take 24 s (per-link timeouts or something else). Decide whether to raise the timeout with a reason or investigate.
The whole file takes about 350 s, and four tests take more than 60 s each against 60-180 s timeouts, so the check CHK-QA-707-AUTH-CRAWL has a long wall-clock time.
Run in parallel with the full suite (as in EV-0006), the file may still time out under memory pressure.
handoff: Run CHK-QA-707-AUTH-CRAWL on a quiet tree. It needs about 6 minutes, so give it a timeout above 350 s. If the dead-links test times out under load, decide whether to raise its 30000 ms timeout and name the reason.
